Requirement: The system shall implement a strict Tenant -> Workspace ownership hierarchy.
The system shall enforce hard Tenant isolation for business data, identities/memberships, API credentials and audit records.
Workspace-owned Decisions and Schemas shall be isolated by default from other Workspaces.
The system shall prohibit direct cross-workspace references and shall permit reuse only through versioned immutable Tenant-level Shared Library assets.
The system shall enforce role and permission checks within Tenant and Workspace scope.
Runtime credentials shall be scoped and shall not authorize access to Decisions outside their permitted Tenant/Workspace scope.
The system shall support credential issuance, revocation and auditable credential lifecycle events.
The system shall allow authorized authors to create and version Decisions within a Workspace.
A Decision shall support a graph composed of Decision Table, Decision Tree, Scripted Expression and Rule Set node types.
The Control Plane shall validate that each Decision Graph is a DAG and shall reject cycles before artifact build/publication.
Runtime shall support topological evaluation and may evaluate dependency-independent branches in parallel while preserving deterministic semantics.
Runtime shall short-circuit graph branches that are not activated by decision conditions.
Node evaluation shall fail-fast by default on contract or computation error.
Authors shall be able to configure a typed default fallback value per eligible node; when configured, a qualifying node exception shall resolve to the fallback and execution may continue.
Graph/node identifiers shall remain traceable across a Decision Version so execution evidence can identify evaluated and matched nodes.
The system shall maintain versioned input and output schemas for Decisions.
Schema fields shall support at least name, data type, required/optional semantics and is_sensitive metadata.
The system shall evaluate schema changes for configured backward/forward compatibility rules and identify breaking changes.
Schema breaking-change status shall contribute to automatic Risk Tier calculation.
Runtime shall validate request payloads against the schema version bound to the selected Decision Version.
An executable artifact and execution evidence shall identify the exact schema version used.
Submitting a release shall trigger automatic Risk Tier calculation; the author shall not be able to self-declare a lower tier.
Risk calculation shall consider change scope, schema breaking-change status and the Decision's production traffic frequency over the previous 30 days.
An authorized Approver may increase a calculated Risk Tier but shall not decrease it.
Tier 1 releases shall require approval by one Domain Approver.
Tier 2 releases shall require sequential approval by Domain Peer Review followed by Workspace Owner approval.
Tier 3 releases shall require quorum including both Domain Owner and Compliance Officer approval.
The author of a release shall be excluded from every approval role for that release.
The system shall record immutable approval/rejection evidence including actor, stage, decision, timestamp and supplied reason/comment where applicable.
Only a release satisfying its required approval policy shall be eligible for production delivery.
The system shall produce an immutable executable artifact from a validated and governed Decision Version.
Artifacts shall include integrity/version metadata sufficient to identify the exact Decision, dependencies, schemas and Shared Library versions.
The system shall support Shadow deployment of an approved candidate against mirrored production inputs.
Shadow candidate results shall not alter or replace the production response.
The system shall capture and expose diff analysis between Active and Shadow outcomes.
The system shall support Canary rollout using deterministic sticky Subject-Key routing.
Sticky percentage routing shall deterministically map the same subject key to the same rollout cohort for a fixed rollout configuration.
The system shall additionally support targeted cohort routing based on configured request attributes/claims.
The system shall support promotion of an eligible candidate to desired Active state.
The system shall support rollback by switching desired Active state to an eligible prior immutable version without cloning that version.
Publish, promotion and rollback actions shall be auditable with actor, from-version, to-version, timestamp and reason where required.
The distribution mechanism shall notify active Runtime nodes of publish/rollback desired-state changes without requiring node restart.
Runtime nodes shall load/validate a new artifact before serving executions from that artifact.
The system shall expose fleet convergence state sufficient to determine desired version and loaded version for active nodes.
Loss of Control Plane connectivity shall not prevent a Runtime node from serving already-loaded eligible artifacts.
The Data Plane shall use bounded eventual consistency for artifact propagation while preserving atomic snapshot execution.
The Data Plane shall expose a production REST evaluation API.
The Data Plane shall expose a production gRPC evaluation API.
Runtime execution nodes shall be stateless with respect to client sessions and long-running process state.
A request shall execute a Decision Graph in one synchronous execution context.
An unpinned request shall execute the latest Active version currently eligible and loaded on the serving node.
The selected Decision Version and all graph dependencies shall be fixed as one atomic snapshot for the lifetime of an execution.
Consumers may request an exact Decision Version using the defined REST header or equivalent gRPC request field.

If the requested pinned version is not eligible/available on the serving Data Plane, REST shall return HTTP 412 Precondition Failed; gRPC shall return a documented semantically equivalent precondition error.
For identical executable snapshot and identical input/context, rule evaluation shall be deterministic.
A successful evaluation response shall include an execution identifier and result; version/trace metadata shall be available according to API contract and authorization.
The system shall capture a Decision Execution Trace Tree identifying evaluated nodes, activated branches, relevant intermediate outcomes and final outcome.
Fields marked is_sensitive shall be masked, tokenized or hashed before trace persistence and shall not be stored as plaintext.
Hot trace storage shall retain full trace trees for a configurable policy within the Sponsor-approved 30-90 day range.
Long-term compliance storage shall retain immutable execution metadata for a configurable policy within the Sponsor-approved 5-7 year range.
Long-term compliance metadata shall include at least ExecutionID, DecisionVersion, InputHash, Output, MatchedNodeIDs, Timestamp and approval/release evidence reference.
Trace and compliance evidence access shall be authorization-scoped and auditable.
Authorized users shall be able to retrieve retained execution evidence by ExecutionID.
Trace capture shall be designed so failure or backpressure of trace persistence does not silently change the business decision result; failure handling shall be observable and policy-controlled.
